caption: : Avg. rate at which the model attends most to each input segment: context, generated response, or other (e.g., system prompts) during generation.
model_annotation: This horizontal stacked bar chart illustrates the average rate at which the model attends most to each input segment—context, generated response, or other (e.g., system prompts)—during generation, comparing two models: “Ours” and “Standard.” The vertical axis lists the two models, while the horizontal axis represents the percentage of attention, ranging from 0% to 100%. Each bar is divided into three colored segments: blue for “Context,” orange for “Generated Response,” and green for “Other,” as indicated by the legend below. For the “Ours” model, attention is distributed as 60.6% to context, 31.7% to generated response, and 7.7% to other. For the “Standard” model, attention is distributed as 23.6% to context, 51.1% to generated response, and 25.3% to other. The chart visually emphasizes that “Ours” allocates significantly more attention to context and less to generated response and other segments compared to “Standard,” suggesting a stronger grounding in context during generation.
